_comment: House style for Icelandic product copy and AI replies. Each rule: id, why, pattern (JavaScript regex source; {LB} and {RB} are letter-safe word edges), flags (default iu), scope (all = every text, product = marketing and product copy only), severity (error or warning), suggest, allowMarker (a line holding this text is allowed), replace (word map for rewriteStyle), examples (bad must hit, good must not). Edit this file to fit your own brand.

rules.why: The long dash reads as machine-made text in Icelandic. Use a comma, a colon, a full stop or brackets.
rules.suggest: comma, colon, full stop or brackets

rules.why: 'Smíðað' and 'smíði' sound stiff for software. Say 'gert' and 'gerð'.
'Skrunaðu' is an awkward loan from 'scroll'. Say 'sjáðu neðar' or just point to the thing.

bad: Skrunaðu niður til að sjá verðin.
good: Sjáðu neðar til að sjá verðin.

rules.why: Product copy says what the product does, not that it is AI. The word stays only in the legally required AI notice, marked on its line.
rules.suggest: say what it does: svarar gestum, tekur bókanir

good: Þú ert að tala við sjálfvirkan aðstoðarmann sem notar gervigreind. [ai-disclosure]

rules.why: 'Spjallmenni' sounds cheap and dated. Say 'aðstoðarmaður' or name the product.
'Lítil fyrirtæki' makes the customer and the product sound small. Leave the size out.
In Iceland a price is quoted as the price. 'Án vsk' and 'með vsk' are never said to a customer.
Honesty is a given, not a feature. Copy says what the product does, never that it does not make things up.
rules.suggest: say what it does for the customer

bad: Svarar eingöngu út frá þínum gögnum.

rules.why: 'Þrjú einföld skref' is a tired sales line.

bad: Byrjaðu í þremur einföldum skrefum. Í 3 einföldum skrefum.

rules.why: Being found on Google is a given, not a selling point.
'Svaraðu bara já' reads as machine-made. Ask the question plainly.
